final.memo:
Bath & Body Works is a standalone powerhouse in personal care and home fragrance, currently suffering from a valuation disconnect that ignores its underlying cash-generative quality [D01], [D04]. While the market fixates on discretionary spending headwinds and interim leadership uncertainty, the company trades at a distressed 5.5x EV/EBITDA multiple, failing to reflect its long-term earnings power [D04], [D05].

Our analysis identifies a clear margin gap of 200 to 470 basis points when benchmarked against high-quality peers like Ulta Beauty and Church & Dwight [D06]. By closing this gap through operational simplification and rigorous cost control, we see a path to a $52.00 target price based on an 8.0x EV/EBITDA re-rating, offering an attractive risk-reward skew [D03], [D06].

The current governance void under interim leadership provides an immediate opportunity for engagement to drive capital allocation discipline and margin expansion [D01], [D07]. We advocate for a permanent CEO appointment with a mandate to execute these operational initiatives, backed by a disciplined share buyback program to capitalize on the current market mispricing [D04], [D07].

We pass on this opportunity today because our thesis lacks the necessary edge. Without an active, differentiated plan for engagement or a specific catalyst beyond the general need for better management, we will wait for clearer signals from the board before committing capital [D01], [D07].
